lastPrompt: there seems to be a bug with kipy not installing onto new machines: [Image #1] - this is on a windows system, the bug may also be present on mac/linux builds.

content.text:
## Findings — kipy bundling broken across all three platforms

The Windows symptom your other Claude session diagnosed is one instance of a **cross-platform problem**: the C++ build installs `zeo-mcp` reliably (via CMake `install` rule), but **kipy bundling is in separate platform-specific shell/PowerShell scripts that can fail or be skipped silently**. A "successful" build can produce a binary that crashes at first import.

### Windows (matches user's screenshot exactly)

| # | File | Issue |
|---|------|-------|
| W1 | `packaging/kicad-win-builder/rebuild_agent.ps1:38-49, 134, 136, 156` | **Hardcoded stale `code\zeo*` paths** from before the monorepo reorg. Auto-detect walks up looking for `code\zeo` — current layout is `src\zeo`. Script either exits with "Could not auto-detect Zeo repo root" or silently no-ops on broken paths. |
| W2 | `packaging/kicad-win-builder/build.ps1` | **Main builder doesn't install kipy at all.** Only `rebuild_agent.ps1` does — and that's a separate manual step. If user runs build.ps1 → NSIS package → installer ships without kipy. |
| W3 | `dev/win_build_installer.ps1:400-404` | `if (Test-Path $KicadPythonDir) { Install-Kipy } else { Log "...skipping." }` — installer built without kipy when path is wrong. No build failure. |
| W4 | `dev/win_build_installer.ps1:394` | `python -m pip install ... 2>&1 \| Out-Null` — silently swallows pip stderr AND exit code. |
| W5 | `dev/win_build_fast.ps1:23` | Still uses old `code\zeo-python` path. |

### macOS

| # | File | Issue |
|---|------|-------|
| M1 | `dev/utils/mac_fast.sh:411-412` | `pip install ... 2>/dev/null \|\| true` — silently swallows pip failures. kipy copied without working deps → ImportError at runtime. |
| M2 | `dev/utils/mac_fast.sh:434-436` | Auto-install fires only if `INTREE_SITE_PKG/kipy` is **completely missing**. Stale/broken installs are never refreshed. |
| M3 | (CMakeLists.txt) | **No CMake install rule for kipy.** Relies on `mac_fast.sh` having been run. `cmake --install` alone produces a bundle without kipy. |

### Linux

| # | File | Issue |
|---|------|-------|
| L1 | `packaging/kicad-appimage/scripts/bundle_kipy.sh:31-34` | `exit 0` when `$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR` missing — AppImage built without kipy, no error. |
| L2 | line 36-38 | KICAD_SOURCE_DIR missing → warn + continue. kipy bundled without proto files → ImportError. |
| L3 | line 77, 81-84, 88 | `pip3 install` calls don't individually verify success. `set -e` catches process failure but pip can exit 0 on partial installs. |

### Root architectural issue

`zeo-mcp` (C++ launcher) and `kipy` (Python package) are produced by **two separate toolchains** with no cross-validation. The launcher is part of the CMake build and goes through `install(TARGETS)`. kipy is bundled by post-build scripts that aren't gated by `zeo-mcp`'s install rule. There's no "verify the bundle is complete" step in any platform's pipeline — a smoke test like `zeo-mcp.exe --version` (or just running it for 100ms) would catch this every time.

### Proposed fix layers (waiting on your direction)

questions.question: How thorough should the fix be?

options.label: Just fix Windows now (most acute)
options.description: Update rebuild_agent.ps1 + win_build_fast.ps1 + win_build_installer.ps1 path references from code\zeo* to src\zeo*, remove silent pip-stderr suppression. ~15 min, no rebuild needed.

options.label: Fix all three platforms' silent failures
options.description: Above + mac_fast.sh: drop `2>/dev/null || true`, force-reinstall kipy each --python pass + bundle_kipy.sh: fail on missing source/protos instead of exit 0. Defensive across the board. ~30 min.

options.label: Above + add smoke-test step to each pipeline
options.description: After bundling, run a quick import check: `python -c "import kipy; from kipy.client import KiCadClient"`. Fails the build loudly if any dep is missing. Catches this class of bug permanently. ~45 min.

options.label: Above + restructure: make kipy a CMake install dependency
options.description: Add a CMake custom target that runs the bundling script and depends on zeo-mcp's install. cmake --install then guarantees kipy is staged. Largest change but eliminates the architectural gap. ~1-2 hours.

lastPrompt: Kipy bundling is borken, why do tool calls in app (when not using the MCP) still work?

content.text:
Now I can answer precisely. **Two different code paths with different search strategies — your in-app tool calls succeed via a fallback that the Windows MCP launcher doesn't have.**

## The two paths

**In-app tool calls** use `KIPY_BOOTSTRAP` (terminal_frame.cpp:59-97). It tries kipy in **three** places, in order:

1. `KICAD_PYTHON_PATH` env var (if set)
2. Walks **6 directory levels up from CWD** looking for `kicad-python/` or `code/kicad-python/` and adds the first match to `sys.path`
3. Plain `import kipy` from the default `sys.path` (site-packages)

It only raises ImportError if all three fail.

**The MCP launcher** (`src/zeo/tools/zeo-mcp/zeo-mcp.cpp:34-40`) is the opposite — *isolated and explicit*:

```cpp
PyConfig_InitIsolatedConfig( &config );
config.use_environment = 0;        // ignores KICAD_PYTHON_PATH and friends
...
config.module_search_paths_set = 1;
PyWideStringList_Append( &config.module_search_paths, lib.c_str() );
PyWideStringList_Append( &config.module_search_paths, dlls.c_str() );
PyWideStringList_Append( &config.module_search_paths, site.c_str() );
```

It deliberately ignores environment variables and only looks at exactly three directories under `bin/`. No fallback walk, no source-tree probing. If `bin/Lib/site-packages/kipy/` doesn't exist, it dies — that's the user's −32000.

## Why your dev machine works

`mac_fast.sh` installs kipy in (at least) two places on your box:

- **In-tree bundle's site-packages** (line 417-418): `cp -R "$KICAD_PYTHON_DIR/kipy" "$INTREE_SITE_PKG/"`
- **Your user's system Python** via editable install (line 424): `python3 -m pip install --break-system-packages --no-deps -e "$KICAD_PYTHON_DIR"`

So path 3 of `KIPY_BOOTSTRAP` resolves — kipy is in site-packages — and the in-app tool call succeeds. Even if site-packages were missing kipy for some reason, the CWD walk in path 2 could still pick it up from your workspace (though note: it searches for `kicad-python`, not `zeo-python`, so post-monorepo-reorg that fallback is actually dead on disk too — but you don't notice because path 3 keeps working).

## Why distribution / Windows users break

Distribution installs ship the binary but rely on the platform packaging script to stage kipy under `bin/Lib/site-packages/`. That step is the one with all the silent-failure paths I listed (Windows W1-W5, macOS M1-M3, Linux L1-L3). When it fails, **both paths** would actually break — but only the MCP one is *visible* because:

- The in-app tool call's `KIPY_BOOTSTRAP` produces a clean JSON diagnostic ImportError ("Failed to import kipy: No module named 'pynng'") that surfaces as a tool error in the chat panel
- The MCP launcher has no equivalent diagnostic — it just exits, and Claude Code translates that into the opaque `-32000`

If the user you're helping had tried an in-app tool call on a fresh prompt (not just a chat prompt), they'd likely see a kipy ImportError in the tool result. They just haven't hit it yet because the crash from earlier (Bug B, SIGPIPE on the dead CC subprocess) happens before they get to that point.

## Summary

| | In-app tool calls | MCP via `zeo-mcp.exe` |
|---|---|---|
| Python env vars honored | ✓ (`KICAD_PYTHON_PATH`) | ✗ (isolated config) |
| Source-tree fallback | ✓ (walks 6 levels) | ✗ |
| site-packages fallback | ✓ | ✓ (only path) |
| Failure surface | JSON diagnostic in tool result | Process exits → `-32000` |

So your observation is correct and consistent with my earlier analysis — the bundling IS broken for distribution builds, but the MCP launcher is the *first* place it bites because it has no slack. The fix should both:
1. Stop the bundling scripts from failing silently (so kipy actually gets staged)
2. Give the MCP launcher equivalent fallbacks (search source tree / honor env vars in dev builds) so a broken bundle doesn't reach end-users without visible warning

## 2. Add a smoke test at the end of `rebuild_agent.ps1`

So that even if all the install steps succeed, a broken kipy is caught before the installer ships:

input.new_string:
# Install mcp SDK (and its transitive deps) for the bundled zeo-mcp.exe launcher
if (-not (Test-Path "$sitePackages\mcp")) {
    Write-Host "  Installing mcp SDK..." -ForegroundColor Gray
    & $pythonBin -m pip install --no-user --target $sitePackages "mcp>=1.0.0"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Write-Host "  mcp SDK install failed!" -ForegroundColor Red
        exit 1
    }
    Write-Host "  mcp SDK installed" -ForegroundColor Gray
} else {
    Write-Host "  mcp SDK already present" -ForegroundColor Gray
}

# Smoke test: confirm the bundle is actually importable. Without this, a
# silently-broken kipy install (missing pynng, stale protos, etc.) ships in
# the installer and surfaces only at runtime as the MCP -32000 error.
# Mirrors the import chain zeo-mcp.exe does on launch.
Write-Host "Verifying kipy import chain..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
$smokeTest = @"
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, r'$sitePackages')
import kipy
from kipy.client import KiCadClient
from kipy.mcp.server import run
print(f'OK: kipy at {kipy.__file__}')
"@
& $pythonBin -c $smokeTest
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    Write-Host "kipy smoke test FAILED. The bundled site-packages is missing modules or has broken protos." -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "  site-packages: $sitePackages" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}
Write-Host "  kipy smoke test passed." -ForegroundColor Gray

function Install-Kipy {
    Log "Installing kipy (KiCad Python bindings)..."

    $kipySource = "$KicadPythonDir\kipy"
    $protoInput = "$KicadSourceDir\api\proto"

    if (-not (Test-Path $kipySource)) {
        Log-Error "kipy package not found at $kipySource"
        exit 1
    }

    # Generate protobuf Python files. Always regenerate so stale builds don't
    # ship outdated bindings against newer .proto definitions.
    Log "Generating protobuf Python files..."
    $protoFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $protoInput -Filter "*.proto" -Recurse | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName
    & $Protoc --python_out="$kipySource\proto" --proto_path=$protoInput @protoFiles
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Log-Error "protoc failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE)"
        exit 1
    }
    python -m protoletariat --dont-create-package --in-place --exclude-google-imports --python-out "$kipySource\proto" protoc --protoc-path $Protoc --proto-path $protoInput @protoFiles
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Log-Error "protoletariat failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE)"
        exit 1
    }

    # Copy kipy package
    if (Test-Path "$sitePackages\kipy") {
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$sitePackages\kipy"
    }
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $sitePackages -Force | Out-Null
    Copy-Item -Recurse $kipySource "$sitePackages\kipy"

    # Install Python dependencies if missing. Don't silence stderr — a silent
    # pip failure here ships an installer with a kipy that ImportErrors on
    # first launch (the bundled zeo-mcp.exe surfaces this as MCP -32000).
    if (-not (Test-Path "$sitePackages\google\protobuf")) {
        Log "Installing Python dependencies..."
        python -m pip install --no-user --target $sitePackages "protobuf>=6.33" "pynng>=0.8.0,<0.9.0" typing_extensions matplotlib cairosvg
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            Log-Error "pip install of kipy dependencies failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE)"
            exit 1
        }
    }

    # Smoke test: confirm the bundle actually imports. Mirrors zeo-mcp.exe's
    # import chain so a broken bundle fails the build, not the user.
    Log "Verifying kipy import chain..."
    $smokeTest = @"
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, r'$sitePackages')
import kipy
from kipy.client import KiCadClient
from kipy.mcp.server import run
print('OK: kipy at', kipy.__file__)
"@
    python -c $smokeTest
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Log-Error "kipy smoke test failed — the staged bundle at $sitePackages is not importable"
        exit 1
    }
    Log "kipy installed and verified."
}

if (-not (Test-Path $KicadPythonDir)) {
    Log-Error "kipy source not found at $KicadPythonDir — refusing to build an installer without kipy"
    exit 1
}

Install-Kipy

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# Bundle kicad-python (kipy) and dependencies into the AppDir.
# This script mirrors the functionality in mac_build_hard.sh for Linux AppImages.
#
# Configuration via environment variables:
#   ENABLE_KIPY_BUNDLE=1          Set to 0 to skip bundling
#   KIPY_SOURCE_DIR=/src/zeo-python   Path to kicad-python source
#   KICAD_SOURCE_DIR=/src/kicad       Path to KiCad/Zeo source (for proto files)
#   APPDIR=/tmp/AppDir                Target AppDir root
#   PYTHON_VERSION=3.11               Python version to target

if [[ "${ENABLE_KIPY_BUNDLE:-1}" != "1" ]]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Skipping (ENABLE_KIPY_BUNDLE!=1)"
    exit 0
fi

APPDIR=${APPDIR:-/tmp/AppDir}
KIPY_SOURCE_DIR=${KIPY_SOURCE_DIR:-/src/zeo-python}
KICAD_SOURCE_DIR=${KICAD_SOURCE_DIR:-/src/kicad}
PYTHON_VERSION=${PYTHON_VERSION:-3.11}

echo "[bundle_kipy] Starting kicad-python bundling"
echo "[bundle_kipy] APPDIR: $APPDIR"
echo "[bundle_kipy] KIPY_SOURCE_DIR: $KIPY_SOURCE_DIR"
echo "[bundle_kipy] KICAD_SOURCE_DIR: $KICAD_SOURCE_DIR"
echo "[bundle_kipy] PYTHON_VERSION: $PYTHON_VERSION"

# Validate source directories
if [ ! -d "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: kicad-python source not found at $KIPY_SOURCE_DIR, skipping"
    exit 0
fi

if [ ! -d "$KICAD_SOURCE_DIR" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: KiCad source not found at $KICAD_SOURCE_DIR, skipping proto copy"
fi

# Determine site-packages location
SITE_PACKAGES="$APPDIR/usr/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages"
LOCAL_SITE_PACKAGES="$APPDIR/usr/local/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages"

# Create directories
mkdir -p "$SITE_PACKAGES"
mkdir -p "$LOCAL_SITE_PACKAGES"

# Copy proto files from KiCad source to kicad-python
if [ -d "$KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Copying protobuf files from KiCad source..."
    mkdir -p "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kicad/api/proto"
    cp -r "$KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto/"* "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kicad/api/proto/"
else
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: Proto files not found at $KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto"
fi

# Install build dependencies (poetry-core for building, mypy-protobuf and protoletariat for proto generation)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing build dependencies..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --quiet poetry-core setuptools mypy-protobuf protoletariat

# Generate Python protobuf bindings
if [ -f "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/tools/generate_protos.py" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Generating Python protobuf bindings..."
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Proto input files:"
    find "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kicad/api/proto" -name "*.proto" 2>/dev/null || echo "  (none found)"
    pushd "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR" > /dev/null
    python3 tools/generate_protos.py
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Generated proto files:"
    find "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kipy/proto" -name "*_pb2.py" 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo "  (none generated)"
    popd > /dev/null
else
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: generate_protos.py not found, skipping proto generation"
fi

# Install kiutils (dependency for kicad-python)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing kiutils..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --target "$SITE_PACKAGES" --upgrade kiutils

# Install kicad-python dependencies
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing kicad-python dependencies..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --target "$SITE_PACKAGES" --upgrade \
    "protobuf>=5.0" \
    "pynng>=0.8.0" \
    typing_extensions

# Install kicad-python itself (without deps, they're already installed)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing kicad-python package..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --target "$SITE_PACKAGES" --no-deps --upgrade --verbose "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR"

# Copy generated proto files directly (pip wheel may not include them)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Copying generated proto files..."
if [ -d "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kipy/proto" ]; then
    cp -r "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kipy/proto/"* "$SITE_PACKAGES/kipy/proto/"
    PB2_COUNT=$(find "$SITE_PACKAGES/kipy/proto" -name '*_pb2.py' | wc -l)
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Copied $PB2_COUNT proto files to $SITE_PACKAGES/kipy/proto/"
fi

# Verify installation
echo "[bundle_kipy] Verifying installation..."
if [ -d "$SITE_PACKAGES/kipy" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] SUCCESS: kipy package installed to $SITE_PACKAGES/kipy"
elif [ -d "$SITE_PACKAGES/kicad" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] SUCCESS: kicad package installed to $SITE_PACKAGES/kicad"
else
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: Could not verify kipy/kicad package installation"
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Contents of $SITE_PACKAGES:"
    ls -la "$SITE_PACKAGES" || true
fi

# Update PYTHONPATH in the environment file
RUNTIME_ENV_FILE="$APPDIR/.env-kipy"
{
    echo "# Generated by bundle_kipy.sh"
    echo "# Source this file in your wrapper script"
    echo "export PYTHONPATH=\"\${APPDIR}/usr/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages:\${APPDIR}/usr/local/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages:\${PYTHONPATH}\""
} > "$RUNTIME_ENV_FILE"

echo "[bundle_kipy] Complete."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# Bundle kicad-python (kipy) and dependencies into the AppDir.
# This script mirrors the functionality in mac_build_hard.sh for Linux AppImages.
#
# Configuration via environment variables:
#   ENABLE_KIPY_BUNDLE=1          Set to 0 to skip bundling
#   KIPY_SOURCE_DIR=/src/zeo-python   Path to kicad-python source
#   KICAD_SOURCE_DIR=/src/kicad       Path to KiCad/Zeo source (for proto files)
#   APPDIR=/tmp/AppDir                Target AppDir root
#   PYTHON_VERSION=3.11               Python version to target

if [[ "${ENABLE_KIPY_BUNDLE:-1}" != "1" ]]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Skipping (ENABLE_KIPY_BUNDLE!=1)"
    exit 0
fi

APPDIR=${APPDIR:-/tmp/AppDir}
KIPY_SOURCE_DIR=${KIPY_SOURCE_DIR:-/src/zeo-python}
KICAD_SOURCE_DIR=${KICAD_SOURCE_DIR:-/src/kicad}
PYTHON_VERSION=${PYTHON_VERSION:-3.11}

echo "[bundle_kipy] Starting kicad-python bundling"
echo "[bundle_kipy] APPDIR: $APPDIR"
echo "[bundle_kipy] KIPY_SOURCE_DIR: $KIPY_SOURCE_DIR"
echo "[bundle_kipy] KICAD_SOURCE_DIR: $KICAD_SOURCE_DIR"
echo "[bundle_kipy] PYTHON_VERSION: $PYTHON_VERSION"

# Validate source directories. We refuse to ship an AppImage that omits kipy:
# the resulting binary would crash on first MCP launch / agent tool call with
# an opaque ImportError, and the build would not have flagged the problem.
if [ ! -d "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] ERROR: kicad-python source not found at $KIPY_SOURCE_DIR" >&2
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Pass KIPY_SOURCE_DIR explicitly or set ENABLE_KIPY_BUNDLE=0 to skip kipy." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -d "$KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] ERROR: KiCad proto sources not found at $KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto" >&2
    echo "[bundle_kipy] kipy needs these to generate its protobuf bindings." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Determine site-packages location
SITE_PACKAGES="$APPDIR/usr/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages"
LOCAL_SITE_PACKAGES="$APPDIR/usr/local/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages"

# Create directories
mkdir -p "$SITE_PACKAGES"
mkdir -p "$LOCAL_SITE_PACKAGES"

# Copy proto files from KiCad source to kicad-python
if [ -d "$KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Copying protobuf files from KiCad source..."
    mkdir -p "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kicad/api/proto"
    cp -r "$KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto/"* "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kicad/api/proto/"
else
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: Proto files not found at $KICAD_SOURCE_DIR/api/proto"
fi

# Install build dependencies (poetry-core for building, mypy-protobuf and protoletariat for proto generation)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing build dependencies..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --quiet poetry-core setuptools mypy-protobuf protoletariat

# Generate Python protobuf bindings
if [ -f "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/tools/generate_protos.py" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Generating Python protobuf bindings..."
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Proto input files:"
    find "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kicad/api/proto" -name "*.proto" 2>/dev/null || echo "  (none found)"
    pushd "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR" > /dev/null
    python3 tools/generate_protos.py
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Generated proto files:"
    find "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kipy/proto" -name "*_pb2.py" 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo "  (none generated)"
    popd > /dev/null
else
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: generate_protos.py not found, skipping proto generation"
fi

# Install kiutils (dependency for kicad-python)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing kiutils..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --target "$SITE_PACKAGES" --upgrade kiutils

# Install kicad-python dependencies
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing kicad-python dependencies..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --target "$SITE_PACKAGES" --upgrade \
    "protobuf>=5.0" \
    "pynng>=0.8.0" \
    typing_extensions

# Install kicad-python itself (without deps, they're already installed)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Installing kicad-python package..."
pip3 install --break-system-packages --target "$SITE_PACKAGES" --no-deps --upgrade --verbose "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR"

# Copy generated proto files directly (pip wheel may not include them)
echo "[bundle_kipy] Copying generated proto files..."
if [ -d "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kipy/proto" ]; then
    cp -r "$KIPY_SOURCE_DIR/kipy/proto/"* "$SITE_PACKAGES/kipy/proto/"
    PB2_COUNT=$(find "$SITE_PACKAGES/kipy/proto" -name '*_pb2.py' | wc -l)
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Copied $PB2_COUNT proto files to $SITE_PACKAGES/kipy/proto/"
fi

# Verify installation
echo "[bundle_kipy] Verifying installation..."
if [ -d "$SITE_PACKAGES/kipy" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] SUCCESS: kipy package installed to $SITE_PACKAGES/kipy"
elif [ -d "$SITE_PACKAGES/kicad" ]; then
    echo "[bundle_kipy] SUCCESS: kicad package installed to $SITE_PACKAGES/kicad"
else
    echo "[bundle_kipy] WARNING: Could not verify kipy/kicad package installation"
    echo "[bundle_kipy] Contents of $SITE_PACKAGES:"
    ls -la "$SITE_PACKAGES" || true
fi

# Update PYTHONPATH in the environment file
RUNTIME_ENV_FILE="$APPDIR/.env-kipy"
{
    echo "# Generated by bundle_kipy.sh"
    echo "# Source this file in your wrapper script"
    echo "export PYTHONPATH=\"\${APPDIR}/usr/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages:\${APPDIR}/usr/local/lib/python${PYTHON_VERSION}/dist-packages:\${PYTHONPATH}\""
} > "$RUNTIME_ENV_FILE"

echo "[bundle_kipy] Complete."

content.text:
## What changed

| File | Fix |
|---|---|
| `packaging/kicad-win-builder/rebuild_agent.ps1` | Path migration `code\zeo*` → `src\zeo*` (auto-detect root, kicad-python dir, proto input, git-describe source); hard-fail if kipy source missing; smoke test at end |
| `dev/win_build_fast.ps1` | Path migration `code\zeo*` → `src\zeo*` |
| `dev/win_build_installer.ps1` | Stop swallowing pip stderr (`2>&1 \| Out-Null` removed); check protoc/protoletariat exit codes; **hard-fail** on missing source instead of "skipping"; smoke test on installer staging |
| `dev/utils/mac_fast.sh` | Stop swallowing pip stderr (`2>/dev/null \|\| true` removed); auto-reinstall trigger now checks pynng/protobuf too, not just `kipy/`; smoke test against bundled Python |
| `packaging/kicad-appimage/scripts/bundle_kipy.sh` | Soft `WARNING ... exit 0` on missing source → hard `ERROR ... exit 1`; same for missing protos; smoke test replaces the "directory exists" check |

## Pattern of all five smoke tests

```python
import kipy
from kipy.client import KiCadClient
from kipy.mcp.server import run
```

This exercises every module the runtime actually loads (kipy core, the pynng-backed `client`, and the MCP server entry point). Any missing dep — protobuf, pynng, mcp SDK, stale protos — surfaces as a build failure, not a runtime crash.

## What's intentionally NOT in this patch

- **The MCP launcher's `Py_InitializeFromConfig` isolation** (zeo-mcp.cpp:28 — `use_environment = 0`). I considered loosening this so it can fall back to env vars / source-tree probes like `KIPY_BOOTSTRAP` does, but that defeats the launcher's point: it's supposed to be deterministic. Stricter is right; the right fix is making sure the bundle is correct, which is what these scripts do now.
- **One-shot remediation script for the user with the broken install.** Separate concern from the build fix; happy to write one if you want.
- **CMake-level integration** (making kipy bundling a dependency of `install(TARGETS zeo-mcp)`). This is the cleanest long-term answer but is a much larger refactor — each platform's bundling logic would need to be invokable from CMake. Worth doing later but not blocking.

Build paths to verify the fix:
- macOS: `./dev/utils/mac_fast.sh --python --install` should now smoke-test and either succeed or fail loudly.
- Windows: `packaging\kicad-win-builder\rebuild_agent.ps1` will exit non-zero if anything is wrong; `dev\win_build_installer.ps1` likewise.
- Linux: `bundle_kipy.sh` will fail the AppImage build instead of warning.

Want me to proceed with the user-side remediation script next, or commit this and stop here?

Another problem that was flagged by a user: OS: Windows 11
Version: 0.2.1

I did an initial install of Zeo and it seems that on first run with default settings, Zeo doesn't create the global library tables. That is, the symbol, footprint, and design block library tables seem to not open properly in the symbol or footprint viewer...

To reproduce, I delete the folder under %appdata%/kicad/10.0 and open Zeo. Zeo will go through the KiCAD init prompts and then drop the user on the board page. Opening the symbol or footprint viewer will show no symbols or footprints available for selection.

If you do install KiCAD 10.0.3 anytime before Zeo is installed, those libraries will be visible; however, since Zeo initializes a invalid library, installing KiCAD after will not fix the problem due to the existence of the library folder.

# Install KiCad symbol and footprint libraries.
# Submodules live at $ZeoRoot directly (kicad-symbols/, kicad-footprints/, ...),
# not under a libraries/ subdir.
$libsBase    = $ZeoRoot
$shareDir    = Join-Path $InstallDir "share\kicad"
$templateDir = Join-Path $shareDir   "template"

if (-not (Test-Path "$shareDir\symbols\Device.kicad_sym")) {
    Write-Host "Installing KiCad symbol libraries..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$shareDir\symbols" -Force | Out-Null
    Copy-Item "$libsBase\kicad-symbols\*.kicad_sym" "$shareDir\symbols\" -Force
    Write-Host "  Installed symbol libraries" -ForegroundColor Gray
} else {
    Write-Host "  Symbol libraries already installed" -ForegroundColor Gray
}

if (-not (Test-Path "$shareDir\footprints")) {
    Write-Host "Installing KiCad footprint libraries..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$shareDir\footprints" -Force | Out-Null
    Copy-Item "$libsBase\kicad-footprints\*.pretty" "$shareDir\footprints\" -Recurse -Force
    Write-Host "  Installed footprint libraries" -ForegroundColor Gray
} else {
    Write-Host "  Footprint libraries already installed" -ForegroundColor Gray
}

# Always (re)write sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table templates with KICAD9->KICAD10
# rewrite. Mirrors the substitution in build.ps1's Start-Prepare-Package.
# Done unconditionally so incremental rebuilds also fix stale templates.
# PS5.1 Set-Content defaults to UTF-16 LE (BOM); KiCad's parser expects UTF-8,
# so always pass -Encoding utf8.
Write-Host "Patching lib-table templates (KICAD9_* -> KICAD10_*)..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
$symTable = Get-Content "$libsBase\kicad-symbols\sym-lib-table" -Raw
$symTable = $symTable -replace 'KICAD9_', 'KICAD10_'
Set-Content "$templateDir\sym-lib-table" $symTable -NoNewline -Encoding utf8
$fpTable = Get-Content "$libsBase\kicad-footprints\fp-lib-table" -Raw
$fpTable = $fpTable -replace 'KICAD9_', 'KICAD10_'
Set-Content "$templateDir\fp-lib-table" $fpTable -NoNewline -Encoding utf8
Write-Host "  Patched sym-lib-table + fp-lib-table" -ForegroundColor Gray

Write-Host "Done!" -ForegroundColor Green

content.text:
## Findings

**Root cause: Zeo deleted upstream KiCad's first-run global-library-table initialization wizard and didn't replace it with anything.**

Evidence:

| Location | What's there | What should be there |
|---|---|---|
| `src/zeo/include/dialogs/panel_global_lib_table_config.h` | Header only — abstract class `PANEL_GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE_CONFIG` declares `GetGlobalTableFileName() = 0` | + `.cpp` files for the per-kiface subclasses (sym, fp, design-block). All missing. |
| `LIBRARY_MANAGER::loadTables()` (library_manager.cpp:64-122) | On missing file: `wxLogTrace("No library table found at ..."); continue;` — no fallback | Should copy from `share/kicad/template/<table>` on first run |
| `LIBRARY_MANAGER::Table(GLOBAL)` (library_manager.cpp:604-614) | Returns `std::nullopt` if not in `m_tables` | (Project scope at line 622 falls back to `createEmptyTable`; GLOBAL has no analogue) |

**Walk-through of the user's repro:**

1. Delete `%appdata%/kicad/10.0/`
2. Launch Zeo → `LIBRARY_MANAGER::LoadGlobalTables()` runs → `loadTables(GetUserSettingsPath(), GLOBAL)` → file doesn't exist → silently skipped → `m_tables` is empty
3. Symbol viewer queries `Table(SYMBOL, GLOBAL)` → `std::nullopt` → empty list

The "KiCad init prompts" the user sees are probably the language/env-var first-launch dialogs, not the library wizard (gone).

**Why "install KiCad first then Zeo" works:** KiCad 10.0.3's wizard populates `%appdata%/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table` for you. Zeo then succeeds at `loadTables()` because the file already exists. Both apps use the same `${KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR}` env var convention so URIs resolve.

**Why "install Zeo first then KiCad" doesn't work:** Once `%appdata%/kicad/10.0/` exists (created by Zeo for its own settings, even with no library table inside), KiCad's own first-run-wizard heuristic probably treats it as "not first run" and skips. The empty global table persists.

## The fix

A single auto-copy in `LIBRARY_MANAGER::LoadGlobalTables()` before the `loadTables()` call: if `GetUserSettingsPath()/<table>` doesn't exist and `GetStockTemplatesPath()/<table>` does, copy template → user path. Quiet, no wizard, just mirrors upstream's "default" behavior without the UI choice. Fixes all three OSes since the bug is in shared code.

Bonus (separate): `packaging/kicad-win-builder/rebuild_agent.ps1:243` has the same monorepo-reorg path bug as the kipy bundling — `$libsBase = $ZeoRoot` should be `$libsBase = Join-Path $ZeoRoot "libraries"`. Affects only dev builds where someone runs `rebuild_agent.ps1` post-monorepo-reorg; the lib-table templates get clobbered with empty content because `Get-Content` on the wrong path returns null.

## Proposed scope

content.text:
## Summary

**Runtime fix** (`library_manager.{cpp,h}`) — applies to all OSes:

- New `LIBRARY_MANAGER::seedGlobalTablesFromTemplates()` helper called from `LoadGlobalTables()` *before* `loadTables()` runs.
- For each of SYMBOL / FOOTPRINT / DESIGN_BLOCK:
  - Skip if the template doesn't exist in `share/kicad/template/` (design-block template doesn't ship in every build — by design)
  - If `%appdata%/kicad/10.0/<table>` doesn't exist → copy template in (fresh install)
  - If it exists but `LIBRARY_TABLE::IsOk()` is false **or** `Rows().empty()` is true → overwrite from template (the 0.2.2-upgrade case)
  - Otherwise leave it alone (user-customized)

So for an existing 0.2.2 user upgrading to 0.2.3, the first launch of 0.2.3:
1. Hits `LoadGlobalTables()` as before
2. Sees that `%appdata%/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table` is missing (0.2.2 never created it) or empty
3. Copies the bundled template into place
4. `loadTables()` then reads the freshly-seeded file and populates `m_tables`
5. Viewers come up with the full bundled library list

**Packaging fix** (`rebuild_agent.ps1`):

- `$libsBase` now correctly points at `$ZeoRoot\libraries\` (monorepo-reorg cleanup, same class of bug as the kipy paths)
- Hard-fail with explicit error if `libraries/` doesn't exist
- Hard-fail with explicit error if `sym-lib-table` / `fp-lib-table` source files are missing or empty (prevents the silent "write empty template, ship installer with broken templates" path)

**What's NOT in this patch:**

- Restoring the full upstream first-run wizard (option 2 you skipped). The auto-copy is silent — users don't see a dialog. If we ever want the choice between default/custom/empty back, that's a follow-up.
- Build-time smoke test for the lib templates analogous to the kipy one. Worth adding to `rebuild_agent.ps1` too — quick `LIBRARY_TABLE`-equivalent parse in PowerShell would catch a malformed template before it ships. Want me to add that as well, or leave it to be caught by the runtime fix (which now overwrites a broken file on launch)?

content.text:
Three test scenarios cover the fix end-to-end. They map to the three real-world states a 0.2.3 user will hit. All can run on your macOS dev box against the installed bundle.

### Setup once

```bash
# 1. Rebuild with the fix
./dev/mac_build.sh --fast --install

# 2. Back up your real settings so you don't nuke your dev config
mv ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0 ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0.dev-backup

# 3. Where the bundled template lives (sanity-check it's there)
TEMPLATE_DIR="/Applications/Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport/template"
# Or for an in-tree install: packaging/kicad-mac-builder/build/kicad-dest/Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport/template
ls "$TEMPLATE_DIR/sym-lib-table" "$TEMPLATE_DIR/fp-lib-table"
```

### Test A — fresh install path (the new-user case)

```bash
# Make sure user settings dir is gone
rm -rf ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0

# Launch Zeo, wait for it to come up, then quit. Don't open a project.
open -W /Applications/Zeo.app   # -W waits for quit

# Expect:
test -s ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table && echo OK sym
test -s ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/fp-lib-table && echo OK fp

# Sym-lib-table should now have ${KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR} rows:
grep -c 'KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR' ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
# Expect ~200+ matches (one per bundled library)
```

Then open Zeo's symbol chooser (Place Symbol → Choose Symbol) — should show the full bundled library tree.

### Test B — 0.2.2 upgrade case (empty file already there)

```bash
rm -rf ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0
mkdir -p ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0

# Simulate the 0.2.2 state: a sym-lib-table file exists but is empty or
# contains just the empty s-expression. Both should trigger the overwrite path.
printf '(sym_lib_table\n)\n' > ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
: > ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/fp-lib-table    # truly empty file

# Snapshot inode + size so we can confirm overwrite happened
stat -f '%i %z' ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
stat -f '%i %z' ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/fp-lib-table

open -W /Applications/Zeo.app

# After quit: file should be much larger and changed
stat -f '%i %z' ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
grep -c 'KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR' ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
```

### Test C — user-customized table (must NOT be clobbered)

```bash
rm -rf ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0
mkdir -p ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0

# A "real" user table — single row, parseable, non-empty
cat > ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table <<'EOF'
(sym_lib_table
  (lib (name "MyOnly")(type "KiCad")(uri "/tmp/nope.kicad_sym")(options "")(descr "user lib"))
)
EOF

# Hash it before
shasum ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table

open -W /Applications/Zeo.app

# After quit: hash must match — file untouched
shasum ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
```

### Log verification (for all three)

```bash
# Find the most recent agent log and grep for the seeding decisions
ls -t ~/Library/Logs/Zeo/agent-*.log | head -1 | xargs grep -E "Seeding global|Replacing empty|already populated"
```

You should see, respectively:

| Test | Expected log line |
|---|---|
| A | `Seeding global sym-lib-table from bundled template (first run)` |
| B | `Replacing empty/invalid global sym-lib-table with bundled template` |
| C | nothing logged (the "already populated" path is `wxLogTrace`, suppressed by default) |

### Cleanup

```bash
rm -rf ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0
mv ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0.dev-backup ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0
```

### What to look for if a test fails

- **A or B file empty after launch** → the template at `SharedSupport/template/` isn't shipping with the bundle, or `GetStockTemplatesPath()` returns a different dir on your build (point at `GetStockTemplatesPath()` log with `WXTRACE=traceLibraries` if you need to confirm)
- **C file got overwritten** → the `IsOk() && !Rows().empty()` discriminator returned false on a valid table. Check by adding a `wxLogInfo` next to the trace in `seedGlobalTablesFromTemplates` to see what it concluded
- **Symbol viewer still empty after A passes** → the table is seeded but the URIs don't resolve. Check `${KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR}` expansion by looking at `Preferences → Configure Paths`; should point at `Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport/symbols/`

The Windows-installer fix (`rebuild_agent.ps1`) you can't unit-test easily from macOS, but it's an additive safety net — the runtime fix is enough on its own for end users. The script change just stops dev builds from shipping empty templates in the first place.

content.text:
`KICAD_TEMPLATE` is `share/kicad/template` — which the symbols/footprints installs populate, and the buggy `rm -rf` then wipes. Removing the `rm` is the correct fix.

## To verify

This change is in `kicad.cmake` which runs as part of the ExternalProject's install step, so you need a real reinstall — not just `--fast`. Since you've been testing with the in-tree build, two options:

### Option 1 — full rebuild (cleanest)

```bash
./dev/mac_build.sh --install
```

That re-runs the install steps including `install-symbols-into-app`, `install-footprints-into-app`, and now-fixed `install-templates-into-app`. Then verify:

```bash
ls -l /Applications/Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport/template/sym-lib-table \
      /Applications/Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport/template/fp-lib-table
```

Both should be non-empty. Then re-run the three test scenarios from before.

### Option 2 — quick patch to your existing install (faster, verifies runtime only)

If you don't want to wait for a full rebuild and just want to verify the runtime auto-copy + the wizard fallback both work end-to-end with templates present:

```bash
# Manually stage the template files into the installed bundle
APP=/Applications/Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport
sudo mkdir -p "$APP/template"
sudo cp libraries/kicad-symbols/sym-lib-table "$APP/template/"
sudo cp libraries/kicad-footprints/fp-lib-table "$APP/template/"

# Fix the KICAD9 → KICAD10 env-var references (mac builder normally does
# this; the win build does it too — both via post-process scripts)
sudo sed -i '' 's/KICAD9_/KICAD10_/g' "$APP/template/sym-lib-table"
sudo sed -i '' 's/KICAD9_/KICAD10_/g' "$APP/template/fp-lib-table"

# Confirm
grep -c KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR "$APP/template/sym-lib-table"   # ~200+
```

Then re-run Test A:

```bash
rm -rf ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0
open -W /Applications/Zeo.app
ls -l ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
grep -c KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
```

If that comes back non-empty and `~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table` exists, both layers are working: the wizard finds templates and/or my auto-copy fires.

## What to look for

| Symptom | Diagnosis |
|---|---|
| Wizard doesn't appear, libs populate silently | `seedGlobalTablesFromTemplates` ran first, wizard saw existing table and skipped. Both layers OK. |
| Wizard appears with "tables could not be found" warning | Templates still aren't in the bundle. Re-check the cmake fix took. |
| Wizard appears without the warning, "Recommended" works | Templates present, wizard fallback works. My auto-copy didn't fire (probably ran before, but the wizard is its own thing). |
| Wizard never appears, libs still empty | Auto-copy fired but maybe template path lookup wrong. Check log for "Seeding global ..." line. |

The wizard and my auto-copy are belt-and-suspenders. The cmake fix is the real underlying bug. Once you've confirmed all three layers work together, you're done.

content.text:
That confirms it. The kicad-dest install **does** have the templates now (32KB `sym-lib-table`), but the in-tree build dir has only the kicad-templates `.kicad_wks` files — never had `sym-lib-table`/`fp-lib-table`. The fix worked for the installer staging dir; you're testing against the wrong app.

## Why this is happening

| Build target | Where | What goes in `SharedSupport/template/` |
|---|---|---|
| **in-tree** (`packaging/kicad-mac-builder/build/kicad/src/kicad-build/kicad/Zeo.app`) | the raw CMake build, used by `mac_fast.sh --fast` + your lldb | only kicad-templates content (worksheets + project dirs). **No sym/fp lib tables.** |
| **kicad-dest** (`packaging/kicad-mac-builder/build/kicad-dest/Zeo.app`) | the post-install bundle, populated by ExternalProject_Add_Step | full content including the now-fixed `sym-lib-table` / `fp-lib-table` |

The `kicad.cmake` fix runs only in the kicad-dest install pipeline. The in-tree build is supposed to be incremental-iteration scaffolding and intentionally doesn't run library install steps (which are slow).

**Test against kicad-dest:**

```bash
rm -rf ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0
open -W packaging/kicad-mac-builder/build/kicad-dest/Zeo.app
ls ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
```

The wizard should appear without the warning, "Recommended" should work, and the sym-lib-table should end up populated.

## Answering the architectural question

> *"is the issue that we are not installing the libraries with zeo or that they are conflicting with an existing kicad10 install. Ideally, it should just use from the same config file (same themes, etc.)"*

It's the former — not installing libraries — and the shared-config goal is already true today; the libraries part just needs to ship correctly. Current state on macOS:

| Resource | KiCad 10.0.3 | Zeo 0.2.x | Shared? |
|---|---|---|---|
| User config dir (themes, paths, hotkeys, colors) | `~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/` | `~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/` | ✅ same path → automatically shared |
| User's `sym-lib-table` / `fp-lib-table` | same dir | same dir | ✅ shared file |
| Bundled symbol/footprint files (`.kicad_sym`, `.pretty/`) | `KiCad.app/Contents/SharedSupport/symbols/` | `Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport/symbols/` | ❌ each app has its own copy |
| `${KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR}` env var (resolves URIs in the shared sym-lib-table) | set at runtime by KiCad → KiCad's bundle path | set at runtime by Zeo → Zeo's bundle path | each app self-resolves |

The interesting bit: **the sym-lib-table itself is portable across both apps** because it uses `${KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR}` which each app expands to its own stock lib path. Library names match (Device, 4xxx, etc.) because both apps ship the same upstream kicad-symbols content. So:

- KiCad installed first → its wizard populates `sym-lib-table` → Zeo (when installed later) reads same file, resolves `${KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR}` to Zeo's own bundle, works.
- Zeo installed first (with templates correctly shipped) → Zeo's wizard populates `sym-lib-table` → KiCad (when installed later) reads same file, resolves to its own bundle, works.

The only way it breaks is if one app's wizard runs but its bundled libraries are missing — which is exactly what you've been hitting because of the `rm -rf template` bug. The cmake.cmake fix closes that hole.

**Could we drop bundling and rely on KiCad's libs?** Could, but it makes Zeo dependent on KiCad being installed — which is a worse first-time UX than shipping libs. The duplication is purely on-disk; runtime behavior is already shared via the env var convention.

## Optional follow-up

If you want the in-tree dev build to also have working libraries for in-place testing without `--install`, the cleanest fix is to symlink kicad-dest's lib dirs into the in-tree bundle in `mac_fast.sh`:

```bash
INTREE_SS="$INTREE_APP/Contents/SharedSupport"
DEST_SS="$BUILDER_DIR/build/kicad-dest/Zeo.app/Contents/SharedSupport"
for d in symbols footprints 3dmodels template; do
    [ -d "$DEST_SS/$d" ] && [ ! -L "$INTREE_SS/$d" ] && \
        ln -sf "$DEST_SS/$d" "$INTREE_SS/$d"
done
```

content.text:
## What changed

| File | Fix |
|---|---|
| `library_manager.cpp` `CreateGlobalTable` | Writes chained URI as `${KICAD10_TEMPLATE_DIR}/sym-lib-table` instead of resolved absolute path. New wizard runs are now portable across app moves / reinstalls / DMG-after-in-tree. |
| `library_manager.cpp` `seedGlobalTablesFromTemplates` | Extended to also auto-repair stale absolute URIs in existing tables — walks `TABLE_TYPE_NAME` rows nicknamed "KiCad", and if the URI is a non-portable absolute path that doesn't resolve, rewrites it to the env-var form and saves. |
| `startwizard_provider_libraries.cpp` `Finish` | Migration path also writes the env-var form for newly-inserted or updated chained rows. |

## Test it on your install right now

You can verify the auto-repair works without rebuilding — just clear and rebuild against the in-tree once more, or test against the DMG you have (which already has the bad sym-lib-table from the wizard).

Actually the cleanest test of the auto-repair specifically:

```bash
# Confirm your current broken state
grep '(lib (name "KiCad")' ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
# Shows: uri "/Users/gmp/workspaces/zeodotdev/zeo/.../in-tree/.../sym-lib-table"

# Rebuild (any build path works — the runtime fix is in the kiface code)
./dev/mac_build.sh --fast --install

# Launch the kicad-dest build
open -W packaging/kicad-mac-builder/build/kicad-dest/Zeo.app

# Re-check the URI
grep '(lib (name "KiCad")' ~/Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/sym-lib-table
# Should now show: uri "${KICAD10_TEMPLATE_DIR}/sym-lib-table"
```

The log should contain:
```
Repairing stale chained URI in global sym-lib-table: '/Users/gmp/...in-tree.../sym-lib-table' -> '${KICAD10_TEMPLATE_DIR}/sym-lib-table'
```

After that, symbol viewer should populate. For a freshly-DMG'd user who has no prior config, the wizard now also writes the portable form from the start, so they never hit this in the first place.

## Wider implication

The DMG you got the original "Nested table not found" error from is fine — it was your *user config* that was bad, written by the in-tree build. Any future Zeo (or KiCad) launch on that machine pre-fix would have hit the same error. After this fix:

- Existing broken installs (yours, anyone who tested an in-tree build then DMG'd) → auto-repair on next launch
- Fresh installs → wizard writes portable URI from the start

For your 0.2.2 → 0.2.3 upgrade testing earlier, the seed-from-template path still handles those users. The two cases are now both covered by the same helper.

function Install-Library {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$True)]
        [Arch]$arch,
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$False)]
        [ValidateSet('Release', 'Debug')]
        [string]$buildType = 'Release',
        [string]$libraryFolderName
    )

    Push-Location (Get-Source-Path $libraryFolderName)

    Set-MSVCEnvironment -Arch $arch -VersionMin $settings.VsVersionMin -VersionMax $settings.VsVersionMax

    $buildName = Get-Build-Name -Arch $arch -BuildType $buildType

    $cmakeBuildFolder = "build/$buildName"

    Write-Host "Installing $libraryFolderName to output" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    & {
        $ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
        cmake --install $cmakeBuildFolder > $null
    }

    if ($LastExitCode -ne 0) {
        Write-Error "Failure with cmake install"
        Pop-Location
        Exit [ExitCodes]::CMakeInstallFailure
    }

    Pop-Location
}

    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(

# Install kipy (the embedded Python bindings) and its runtime dependencies
# into the staged Python's site-packages. The bundled zeo-mcp.exe launcher
# does `from kipy.mcp.server import run` on startup — without this step the
# installer ships an empty Lib/site-packages and the user gets the opaque
# MCP -32000 error on first launch.
#
# Historically this was the job of the dev-only rebuild_agent.ps1 which was
# expected to be run manually after build.ps1 — that's how 0.2.2 shipped
# without kipy. Bringing it inline here makes the main release pipeline
# self-contained and the smoke test guards against silent pip failures.
function Install-Kipy-Bundle {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$True)]
        [string]$destBin,
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$True)]
        [string]$pythonBin,
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$True)]
        [string]$protoc
    )

    $zeoRoot        = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..")
    $kicadPythonDir = Join-Path $zeoRoot "src\zeo-python"
    $kipySource     = Join-Path $kicadPythonDir "kipy"
    $kicadSourceDir = Join-Path $zeoRoot "src\zeo"
    $protoInput     = Join-Path $kicadSourceDir "api\proto"
    $sitePackages   = Join-Path $destBin "Lib\site-packages"

    if (-not (Test-Path $kipySource)) {
        Write-Error "kipy source not found at $kipySource. Cannot package an installer without kipy."
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    if (-not (Test-Path $protoInput)) {
        Write-Error "Zeo proto sources not found at $protoInput"
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    if (-not (Test-Path $protoc)) {
        Write-Error "protoc not found at $protoc (vcpkg protobuf package may not be installed)"
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    # Generate protobuf Python files (always regenerate to pick up proto changes
    # across versions; stale bindings against newer .proto can ImportError at runtime).
    Write-Host "Generating kipy protobuf bindings..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Push-Location $kicadPythonDir
    & $pythonBin tools\generate_protos.py --protoc $protoc --input $protoInput --output "$kipySource\proto"
    $protoExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    Pop-Location
    if ($protoExit -ne 0) {
        Write-Error "Proto generation failed (exit $protoExit)"
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    # Generate kipy/kicad_api_version.py from `git describe`. Mirrors what
    # src/zeo-python/build.py does during a wheel build; we bypass build.py
    # here so we replicate the step inline. Without this,
    # `from kipy.kicad_api_version import KICAD_API_VERSION` fails at runtime.

# Install kipy (the embedded Python bindings) and its runtime dependencies
# into the staged Python's site-packages. The bundled zeo-mcp.exe launcher
# does `from kipy.mcp.server import run` on startup — without this step the
# installer ships an empty Lib/site-packages and the user gets the opaque
# MCP -32000 error on first launch.
#
# Historically this was the job of the dev-only rebuild_agent.ps1 which was
# expected to be run manually after build.ps1 — that's how 0.2.2 shipped
# without kipy. Bringing it inline here makes the main release pipeline
# self-contained and the smoke test guards against silent pip failures.
function Install-Kipy-Bundle {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$True)]
        [string]$destBin,
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$True)]
        [string]$pythonBin,
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$True)]
        [string]$protoc
    )

    $zeoRoot        = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..")
    $kicadPythonDir = Join-Path $zeoRoot "src\zeo-python"
    $kipySource     = Join-Path $kicadPythonDir "kipy"
    $kicadSourceDir = Join-Path $zeoRoot "src\zeo"
    $protoInput     = Join-Path $kicadSourceDir "api\proto"
    $sitePackages   = Join-Path $destBin "Lib\site-packages"

    if (-not (Test-Path $kipySource)) {
        Write-Error "kipy source not found at $kipySource. Cannot package an installer without kipy."
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    if (-not (Test-Path $protoInput)) {
        Write-Error "Zeo proto sources not found at $protoInput"
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    if (-not (Test-Path $protoc)) {
        Write-Error "protoc not found at $protoc (vcpkg protobuf package may not be installed)"
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    # Generate protobuf Python files (always regenerate to pick up proto changes
    # across versions; stale bindings against newer .proto can ImportError at runtime).
    Write-Host "Generating kipy protobuf bindings..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Push-Location $kicadPythonDir
    & $pythonBin tools\generate_protos.py --protoc $protoc --input $protoInput --output "$kipySource\proto"
    $protoExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    Pop-Location
    if ($protoExit -ne 0) {
        Write-Error "Proto generation failed (exit $protoExit)"
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    # src/zeo-python/build.py does during a wheel build; we bypass build.py
    # here so we replicate the step inline. Without this,
    # `from kipy.kicad_api_version import KICAD_API_VERSION` fails at runtime.
    Write-Host "Generating kipy/kicad_api_version.py..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $gitDescribe = (& git -C $kicadSourceDir describe --long 2>$null)
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($gitDescribe)) {
        $shortSha = (& git -C $kicadSourceDir rev-parse --short HEAD 2>$null)
        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($shortSha)) {
            $shortSha = "unknown"
        }
        $gitDescribe = "0.0.0-0-g$($shortSha.Trim())"
    }
    $gitDescribe = $gitDescribe.Trim()
    $apiVersionFile = Join-Path $kipySource "kicad_api_version.py"
    @"
# This file is automatically generated, do not modify it
KICAD_API_VERSION = "$gitDescribe"
"@ | Set-Content -Path $apiVersionFile -Encoding utf8
    Write-Host "  KICAD_API_VERSION = $gitDescribe" -ForegroundColor Gray

    # Stage the kipy package itself into site-packages. Always replace so
    # an incremental build picks up source changes.
    Write-Host "Staging kipy package into site-packages..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    if (Test-Path "$sitePackages\kipy") {
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$sitePackages\kipy"
    }
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $sitePackages -Force | Out-Null
    Copy-Item -Recurse $kipySource "$sitePackages\kipy"

    # Install kipy's runtime dependencies. Unconditional so this doesn't
    # short-circuit on a stale partial install (which is how the 0.2.2
    # builds shipped with `kipy/` present but `google/`, `pynng/` and
    # `sniffio/` missing). Hard-fail rather than silently swallow.
    Write-Host "Installing kipy runtime dependencies..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    & $pythonBin -m pip install --no-user --target $sitePackages --upgrade `
        "protobuf>=6.33" "pynng>=0.8.0,<0.9.0" typing_extensions "mcp>=1.0.0" "Pillow>=10.0"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Write-Error "pip install of kipy runtime dependencies failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE)"
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }

    # Smoke test: confirm the staged bundle actually imports. Mirrors the
    # import chain zeo-mcp.exe and the in-app agent run-shell perform on
    # launch — any missing module (pynng, google.protobuf, sniffio,
    # anyio, etc.) fails the build now instead of the user later.
    Write-Host "Verifying kipy import chain..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $smokeTest = @"
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, r'$sitePackages')
import kipy
from kipy.client import KiCadClient
from kipy.mcp.server import run
print('OK: kipy at', kipy.__file__)
"@
    & $pythonBin -c $smokeTest
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        Write-Error "kipy smoke test failed — staged site-packages at $sitePackages is not importable. Refusing to package."
        Exit [ExitCodes]::KipyInstallFailure
    }
    Write-Host "  kipy bundle staged and verified." -ForegroundColor Green
}

content.text:
## Summary

**Root cause for 0.2.2 Windows installs missing deps:** the main release pipeline (`packaging/kicad-win-builder/build.ps1`) **never installed kipy or its runtime dependencies at all**. kipy install was only in `rebuild_agent.ps1`, a dev-only script that wasn't part of the CI/release flow. So when 0.2.2 was packaged, NSIS happily bundled a `Lib/site-packages` that had only the wxPython/extra-requirements deps (line 1204 in build.ps1), missing kipy / google.protobuf / pynng / mcp transitive deps.

**Why mac side has no complaints:** `dev/utils/mac_fast.sh` (and its `install_kipy()` function) IS the main mac build pipeline. macOS users get the kipy install as part of every build. Windows split the responsibility between two scripts and only one was wired into CI.

**What I changed:**

| File | Fix |
|---|---|
| `packaging/kicad-win-builder/build.ps1` | New `Install-Kipy-Bundle` function (~120 lines). Generates proto bindings, writes `kicad_api_version.py`, copies `kipy/` into `Lib/site-packages/`, `pip install`'s `protobuf>=6.33`, `pynng>=0.8.0,<0.9.0`, `typing_extensions`, `mcp>=1.0.0`, `Pillow>=10.0` (mirrors the declared deps in `src/zeo-python/pyproject.toml`), then runs a smoke test that imports the same modules `zeo-mcp.exe` does. Called from `Start-Prepare-Package` after the library installs. Skipped only on cross-compile builds (with a loud warning to run `rebuild_agent.ps1` separately). |
| `packaging/kicad-win-builder/KiBuild/KiBuild.psm1` | New `KipyInstallFailure = 29` exit code so build.ps1 exits cleanly on any kipy step failure. |

**What this catches that the old setup missed:**
- Silent pip failures — `$LASTEXITCODE` checked after every step, hard-fail
- Stale partial installs — `--upgrade` flag forces reinstall, no more "skip if `google/protobuf` already exists" pathological gate
- Wrong-arch / corrupted modules — smoke test imports `kipy`, `KiCadClient`, `kipy.mcp.server.run` at the end. Catches missing pynng, missing google.protobuf, broken proto bindings, missing sniffio/anyio
- Stale source paths from monorepo reorg — uses `Resolve-Path "$PSScriptRoot\..\.."` to find the monorepo root, no hardcoded `code\zeo*`

**About `grpc_tools` in the user's missing-deps list:** kipy's `pyproject.toml` doesn't declare `grpc_tools` as a runtime dep, and `grep` shows no `import grpc_tools` in kipy source. It's a build-time-only dep for protobuf generation. If anything else in the agent actually needs it at runtime, point me at it and I'll add it; otherwise the user's list may have an extra entry there.

**For 0.2.2 users with missing deps right now:** they should upgrade to 0.2.3 once it ships. The NSIS installer wipes `bin/Lib/` before reinstalling (install.nsi:360), so the upgrade itself will replace the broken site-packages with a now-verified one.

**What's NOT in this patch:**
- A standalone remediation script for users to repair their 0.2.2 install in-place. Possible to write but probably noise — the 0.2.3 NSIS installer's upgrade path already handles it.
- Cross-compile (arm64-on-x64) kipy bundling. Currently skipped with a warning pointing at `rebuild_agent.ps1`. Real cross-compile support would need `pip install --platform` plumbing; deferring until someone needs an arm64 release.

Want me to also write the 0.2.2 → 0.2.3 in-place remediation script as a backup for users who can't / won't reinstall?

== Readme
This repo contains all the tooling to build and package KiCad for releases.

The builder is composed of PowerShell scripting that allows us to build native Windows logic to handle the build process
and breaking it down to steps/functions that can be individually debugged.

=== Prerequisites

These are the requirements before the repository can be used.

- Microsoft Visual Studio 2019 or newer (IDE or Build Tools)
- Windows 10, Windows Sever 2019 or newer (PowerShell 5.1+ required)
- "Git for Windows" client

=== Building KiCad

`build.ps1` is the sole script that has various switches and args that break down the build process into
multiple steps.

==== Supported Architectures
Currently the following architectures are officially supported:

- x86
- x64

Stubbing is present for:

- arm
- arm64

but they will not build due to dependency issues.

==== Build Steps

===== Initialize the builder
This fetches any additional dependency tools we require for building that will be stored within the builder package structure

`.\build.ps1 -Init`

===== Build Vcpkg
This initializes vcpkg if required and builds the latest required dependencies for KiCad
`.\build.ps1 -Vcpkg -Latest -Arch x64`

===== Build KiCad
This builds the latest version of KiCad master
`.\build.ps1  -Build -Latest -Arch x64 -BuildType Release`

===== Package KiCad
`.\build.ps1 -Package -Arch x64 -BuildConfigName ${params.BUILD_CONFIG} -Lite -Prepare $True`



=== Extra Functions

==== Symbols

`symbols.ps1` provides management functionality of KiCad's symbol storage. 
This is intended for https://symbols.kicad.org and is simply a helper to invoke `symstore` and `agestore` to update symbols.

It can be tested locally easily by placing a zip file containing pdbs into a new subfolder, in this example it will be called `.artifacts` as used
by our jenkins process

`.\symbols.ps1 -Publish -SourceZipPath \.artifacts\ -SymbolStore <localdiskpathtostorefiles>`

== Credits
- Brian Sidebotham who started the win-builder long ago in 2015
- Nick Østergaard who took over from Brian and maintained it for many years later and expanding it's abilities while msys2 was still used
- Mark Roszko who took over and transitioned the project to MSVC builds with enhanced scripting

content.text:
Here's the canonical Windows build process for shipping 0.2.3 with the kipy-bundling fix:

## Prereqs (on the build machine)

- Windows 10/11 (PowerShell 5.1+)
- Visual Studio 2019+ (IDE or Build Tools — needs MSVC)
- Git for Windows
- ~30 GB free disk (vcpkg ports take real space)

## Step 1 — Create the 0.2.3 build config

Copy the 0.2.1 config and bump the version:

```powershell
cd packaging\kicad-win-builder\build-configs
Copy-Item zeo-0.2.1.json zeo-0.2.3.json
# Then edit zeo-0.2.3.json: "Zeo 0.2.3" + "0.2.3"
```

## Step 2 — One-time setup (skip if already done on this machine)

```powershell
cd packaging\kicad-win-builder

# Downloads CMake, Ninja, NSIS, vcpkg, etc. into .support/  (~5 min)
.\build.ps1 -Init

# Optional: point at a pre-existing vcpkg checkout instead of cloning local
# .\build.ps1 -Config -VcpkgPath="C:\path\to\vcpkg"
```

## Step 3 — Build sequence (run in order)

```powershell
# Build vcpkg deps (~30 min first time, cached afterwards)
.\build.ps1 -Vcpkg -Latest -Arch x64 -BuildConfigName zeo-0.2.3

# Build Zeo's C++ source (~20 min)
.\build.ps1 -Build -Latest -Arch x64 -BuildType Release -BuildConfigName zeo-0.2.3

# Stage + create the NSIS installer.
# THIS is where the new Install-Kipy-Bundle hook runs.
.\build.ps1 -Package -Arch x64 -BuildConfigName zeo-0.2.3 -Prepare $True
```

## Step 4 — Verify the smoke test fired

In the `-Package` step output, look for this block (it's the new code):

```
Generating kipy protobuf bindings...
Generating kipy/kicad_api_version.py...
Staging kipy package into site-packages...
Installing kipy runtime dependencies...
Verifying kipy import chain...
OK: kipy at C:\...\Lib\site-packages\kipy\__init__.py
  kipy bundle staged and verified.    [Green]
```

If any of those fail the build exits with code `29` (`KipyInstallFailure`) — **the installer will NOT be produced**. That's the whole point of the smoke test; we'd rather fail the build than ship a broken installer.

## Step 5 — Artifact location

```
packaging\kicad-win-builder\.out\zeo-0.2.3-<buildname>\zeo-0.2.3-x64.exe
```

That .exe is the NSIS installer to upload to your release page.

## Sanity-check the produced installer locally before publishing

Spot-check the `.out` staging dir before NSIS packaging to confirm site-packages got everything:

```powershell
$staged = "packaging\kicad-win-builder\.out\zeo-0.2.3-x64-Release\bin\Lib\site-packages"
"kipy", "google", "pynng", "mcp", "anyio", "sniffio" | ForEach-Object {
    if (Test-Path "$staged\$_") {
        "OK   $_"
    } else {
        "MISS $_"
    }
}
```

Then install the resulting .exe in a VM (or your own machine if you're brave), open Claude Code, set up MCP, and confirm zeo-mcp doesn't error -32000.

## What's intentionally different from before

- **Old 0.2.2 flow**: `build.ps1` ran end-to-end without ever installing kipy. Whoever was packaging had to remember to run `rebuild_agent.ps1` separately. Easy to forget — and they did, which shipped 0.2.2 broken.
- **New 0.2.3 flow**: `build.ps1 -Package` includes kipy bundling and smoke test automatically. There's nothing extra to remember; if the build succeeds the bundle is verified working.

`rebuild_agent.ps1` still exists for dev incremental rebuilds (faster than re-running the full pipeline), but it's no longer load-bearing for release builds.

## A note on the BuildConfigName arg

`-BuildConfigName zeo-0.2.3` tells the script which JSON in `build-configs/` to load. That JSON sets the version string baked into the NSIS installer name + the bundle's About dialog. If you skip the flag it defaults to `kicad-nightly`, which would produce an installer named after KiCad nightly — almost certainly not what you want.

Want me to also add a `Verify` switch to `build.ps1` (like `.\build.ps1 -Verify -Arch x64 -BuildConfigName zeo-0.2.3`) that just re-runs the smoke test against an already-built `.out` dir without rebuilding? Useful for "did my fix actually land in the artifact" sanity checks without doing a 50-min full rebuild.

content.text:
Right — two distinct issue groups, both addressed in this session but with different scopes. Here's the status:

## Issue 1 — Build dependencies (MCP -32000 + random crash origin)

The dep-bundling bugs explain both visible symptoms:
- **MCP -32000**: zeo-mcp.exe can't find kipy / its deps → subprocess dies on import → MCP client sees -32000
- **Random Windows crashes on prompt**: Claude Code backend writes to dead MCP stdin pipe → SIGPIPE → process aborts (the "instant crash to desktop" symptom)

So fixing the build deps cuts the root. But there's also runtime hardening that's still worth doing, since *any* future dep regression would re-create the SIGPIPE/spawnWorker crash even if the bundle is correct.

| Status | What |
|---|---|
| ✅ Done | `build.ps1`: new `Install-Kipy-Bundle` function with smoke test, wired into `Start-Prepare-Package` |
| ✅ Done | `KiBuild.psm1`: `KipyInstallFailure = 29` exit code |
| ✅ Done | `rebuild_agent.ps1`: `code\zeo*` → `src\zeo*` paths, hard-fail on missing source, smoke test |
| ✅ Done | `dev/win_build_fast.ps1`, `dev/win_build_installer.ps1`: path migration + stop swallowing pip stderr + smoke test |
| ✅ Done | `dev/utils/mac_fast.sh`: stop swallowing pip stderr, check pynng+protobuf in auto-reinstall trigger, smoke test |
| ✅ Done | `packaging/kicad-appimage/scripts/bundle_kipy.sh`: hard-fail on missing source, smoke test |
| ⚠ Not done | **SIGPIPE not ignored anywhere** — `signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN)` at startup in `pgm_base.cpp`. Defensive: stops any future "MCP subprocess died → write() → crash" from taking down the app even if a different dep ever goes missing |
| ⚠ Not done | **`spawnWorker` exception escape** — `AGENT_CLOUD_SYNC::spawnWorker` and `USAGE_SYNC::spawnWorker` construct `std::thread` directly from the lambda without try/catch. Any uncaught exception in cURL/JSON/file I/O → `std::terminate` → process abort. Should be wrapped at thread boundary |

## Issue 2 — Libraries not installing correctly (separate cause)

This was *not* the same root cause as Issue 1 — it had three independent contributing bugs across platforms.

| Status | What |
|---|---|
| ✅ Done | `library_manager.cpp`: `seedGlobalTablesFromTemplates()` runs in `LoadGlobalTables()` — handles fresh install, 0.2.2 upgrade (missing/empty table), AND stale-absolute-URI repair (the in-tree-build-then-DMG case) |
| ✅ Done | `library_manager.cpp` `CreateGlobalTable`: writes portable `${KICAD10_TEMPLATE_DIR}/sym-lib-table` instead of resolved absolute path |

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   This was an extensive debugging and fix session for Zeo (a KiCad fork) addressing multiple distinct bugs:
   
   - **Bug 1**: PCB agent tool calls (`pcb_get_summary`, `pcb_inspect`) timing out at 120s on macOS. Started as "tool calls don't seem to work, they just time out."
   - **Bug 2**: Stackup tool returning wrong layer count (copper_layers: 2 for a 4-layer board)
   - **Bug 3**: App crashing instantly on Windows when users send any prompt — "instant crash to desktop"
   - **Bug 4**: MCP connection error: "no kipy found"
   - **Bug 5**: Windows 11 / Zeo 0.2.1 fresh install showing empty symbol/footprint viewers
   - **Bug 6**: DMG install showing "Nested table '...SharedSupport/template/sym-lib-table' not found" error
   - **Bug 7**: 0.2.2 Windows installs missing dependencies (kipy, google, grpc_tools, pynng, sniffio)
   - **Bug 8 (current)**: User wants library tables to auto-fall-back to existing KiCad install when Zeo's are missing, with polite "using KiCad install at X" notice instead of error
   
   User preferences/constraints (saved memory): "Propose findings before patching - for 'find bugs' requests, list findings + ask, don't edit"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - wxWidgets event loop (`YieldFor` vs `wxYield`, `ProcessPendingEvents`, event categories)
   - KiCad IPC API server (single-threaded main-loop dispatching, nng/pynng REQ/REP sockets)
   - Embedded Python in C++ apps (PyRun_StringFlags, GIL management)
   - Library table chain-loading (TABLE_TYPE_NAME rows with URI references)
   - Environment variable URI substitution (`${KICAD10_TEMPLATE_DIR}`, `${KICAD10_SYMBOL_DIR}`)
   - Cross-platform packaging: CMake ExternalProject, NSIS installers, AppImage, macOS DMG
   - Python dependency bundling with pip --target
   - Monorepo path migration (`code/zeo*` → `src/zeo*`)
   - SIGPIPE on POSIX (default termination behavior)
   - std::thread exception escape → std::terminate

3. Files and Code Sections:
   
   - **src/zeo/include/api/api_server.h**: Added `ProcessPendingRequests()` declaration for draining IPC queue from spin loops.
   
   - **src/zeo/common/api/api_server.cpp**: Implementation:
     ```cpp
     void KICAD_API_SERVER::ProcessPendingRequests()
     {
         while( m_hasQueuedRequests.load() )
             processNextQueuedRequest();
     }
     ```
   
   - **src/zeo/agent/agent_frame.cpp**: Added `wx/app.h` include and two drains in `SendRequest` spin loop (around line 3150):
     ```cpp
     if( Pgm().HasApiServer() )
         Pgm().GetApiServer().ProcessPendingRequests();
     if( wxTheApp )
         wxTheApp->ProcessPendingEvents();
     ```
   
   - **src/zeo/agent/tools/python/pcb/pcb_inspect.py**: Stackup section rewritten to count copper from `stackup.layers` and sum thickness directly (working around `calculate_board_thickness()` under-reporting dielectrics).

     - Added `seedGlobalTablesFromTemplates()` (~85 lines) called from `LoadGlobalTables()`
     - Handles fresh install, 0.2.2 upgrade (empty/missing file), AND stale absolute URI repair
     - Modified `CreateGlobalTable` to write portable URI:

       chained.SetURI( wxString::Format( wxT( "${%s}/%s" ),
                                         ENV_VAR::GetVersionedEnvVarName( wxT( "TEMPLATE_DIR" ) ),
                                         tableFileName( aType ) ) );
       ```

     - Generates protobuf bindings

     ```cpp
     wxString PATHS::FindExternalKiCadTemplatesPath()
     {
         std::vector<wxString> candidates;
     #if defined( __WXMAC__ )
         candidates.push_back( wxT( "/Applications/KiCad/KiCad.app/Contents/SharedSupport/template" ) );
     #elif defined( __WXMSW__ )
         candidates.push_back( wxT( "C:\\Program Files\\KiCad\\10.0\\share\\kicad\\template" ) );
         candidates.push_back( wxT( "C:\\Program Files\\KiCad\\9.0\\share\\kicad\\template" ) );

We had a few issues: Some users ran into errors where the application would randomly crash when running the agent app. This seemed to be correlated with the zeo-mcp not working, the root cause of both being the build dependancies. Namely: in "C:\Program Files\Zeo\0.2.2\bin\Lib\site-packages". kipy, google, grpc_tools, pynng and sniffio are missing. Then there is the seperate issue of the libraries not installing correctly. The github issue is: OS: Windows 11
Version: 0.2.1

I did an initial install of Zeo and it seems that on first run with default settings, Zeo doesn't create the global library tables. That is, the symbol, footprint, and design block library tables seem to not open properly in the symbol or footprint viewer...

To reproduce, I delete the folder under %appdata%/kicad/10.0 and open Zeo. Zeo will go through the KiCAD init prompts and then drop the user on the board page. Opening the symbol or footprint viewer will show no symbols or footprints available for selection.

If you do install KiCAD 10.0.3 anytime before Zeo is installed, those libraries will be visible; however, since Zeo initializes a invalid library, installing KiCAD after will not fix the problem due to the existence of the library folder.. The current changes in git were supposed to fix both, however I don't think they accomplish that/ are very messy. Read them, I will delete the changes, and then we will make all the clean fixes
